**Visual Analysis:**

- **Plant part affected**: Banana leaf (large, broad leaf with parallel veins — characteristic Musa/banana plant)
- **Color pattern**: Pronounced yellowing/chlorosis starting at the leaf margins and base, progressing inward toward the midrib; the central portions remain relatively greener
- **Texture/pattern**: The yellowing is diffuse and systemic (gradient-like), not showing discrete oval spots or dark necrotic lesions
- **Distribution**: Asymmetric yellowing — one side and the basal area are more severely affected; the discoloration has a "spreading inward from margins" appearance

**Differential Reasoning:**

| Class | Fits? | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **Panama Disease** | ✅ Strong | Marginal yellowing spreading inward; systemic chlorosis on banana leaf; older leaves affected first — classic Fusarium wilt pattern |
| Yellow_And_Black_Sigatoka | Partial | Sigatoka typically shows discrete streaks/oval spots with yellow halos, not this diffuse marginal yellowing |
| Cordana_Leaf_Spot | No | Shows distinct oval lesions with brown centers; not present here |
| Bunchy_Top | No | Virus causes narrow, erect, bunching leaves with dark green streaks on petioles |
| Cigar_End_Rot | No | Affects fruit tips, not leaves |
| Anthracnose | No | Dark sunken lesions; no discrete black/brown spots seen here |

**Conclusion**: The diffuse marginal yellowing progressing inward on a banana leaf — without discrete spots, streaks, or lesions — is the hallmark presentation of **Panama Disease** (Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. cubense), where systemic vascular infection causes leaves to yellow from the margins inward and eventually collapse.
